- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% for 30-day horizons.
- After a price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” penalty: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±2% of recent 7-day moving average.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in late forecast windows; for 30-day forecasts, add a 1–2% upward bias if recent 10-day average is below 38.00.
- If true outcome shows a sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply a “trend decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for 5–7 days following a >10% drop.
